_doc: Medium batch m06 themed pass (Opus): seals, otters, ship rats, leeches and the garfish. Every creature has its own signature motif (module claude/pf-anim/motifs/medium_m06.js, 26 motifs; five signatures bring a custom chain effect: pup raft, otter belly slide, rats on a hawser, inch-looping leech, skipping garfish). One small motif is reused where truly the same (rot-spit for the ship rats' bilge). Sibling sharing: the two seals share flipper-splash; the four leeches share leech-sucker (every Latch piece) and leech-gorge (feeding / drain pieces), and bog / giant / tiger leeches share leech-loop as a secondary motif, each with its own palette and speed. All 8 pieces per creature carry a hand note.

seal-pup-raft.notes: A raft of round white harp-seal pups with huge dark eyes, bobbing together off a rocky coast; they slap the water with their little flippers and squeak.

u0.n: Pup Slap: little foreflippers rear up and slap flat on the water, a fan of splash drops flies off the edge

p.u1: Blubber Cover: the pups huddle shoulder to shoulder along the edge, blinking, the swell rocking under them

u2.n: Whisker Squeak: pup muzzles pop out and back, whiskers fanning wide, squeak bursts startling the foe

u3.n: Raft Shove: the whole raft of pups shoves out and drops back with a slosh, bubbles rising

b0.n: Whisker Nip: bristling muzzles lunge off the edge and nip, squeak rays popping

b1.n: Raft Belly-Flop: flippers slap down one after another, splash and bubbles thrown up

b2.n: Blubber Slick: the pups line the edge, white fluff glistening wet with sheen flecks

b3.n: Rock-Slide Dive: pups slide off the rock one by one and plop into the water, bubbles

ice-floe-seal.notes: A heavy grey bull seal with a thick scarred neck that hauls out on the ice floes of the tundra coast; galumphs on its belly and flies into a rage when cornered.

u0.n: Floe Bash: a tilted ice floe slab slams out of the edge and drops back, the blue crack widening, snow kicked up

u1.n: Ice Shove: the scarred bull shoves out neck-first and drops back, angry marks popping (enrage)

u2.n: Fat Wall: grey bulls lie flank to flank along the edge, thick necks and blubber rolling as they breathe

p.u3: Haul Out: the seals galumph out onto the ice and hump back, snow flicked up behind

b0.n: Floe-Edge Snap: a thick-necked seal lunges off the floe edge and snaps

b1.n: Haul-Out Splash: heavy flippers slap the water as the bull hauls out, splash drops flying

b2.n: Oily Floe-Hide: ice floes line up along the edge, an oily sheen flicking over them

b3.n: Overboard Sweep: floe slabs tip off the edge and slide down into the sea, snow falling

river-otter.notes: A sleek brown river otter with bristling whiskers that toboggans down muddy banks on its belly, plays tug and toss with fish and stacks the bank with sticks and stones.

p.u0: Slide Tackle: otters shoot belly-first off the edge, whiskers forward; the chain is a belly slide down a wet mud streak
p.u1: Bank Dam: sticks and stones stack up along the edge one by one, an otter head peeking over the top

u2.n: Fish Toss: silver fish flip end over end between spots, tied by the arc of the throw

u3.n: Belly Slide: otters slide out on a glossy mud streak and swoop back

b0.n: Belly-Slide Snap: one otter toboggans the length of the edge and snaps at the end, bubbles

b1.n: Stream Rock Splash: stones from the bank tumble off the edge into the stream, bubbles rising

b2.n: Slippery Mud Sheen: otters lie along a glossy wet mud streak on the edge

b3.n: Playful Stream Tug: otters hang at spots tied by a line of stream water, tugging back and forth

ship-rat-crew.notes: A crew of black ship rats with bead eyes and long pink tails: they run the hawsers, swing on the ropes, gnaw the hold and shove the gangplank; smells of tar and bilge.

u0.n: Gangplank Shove: a nailed wooden gangplank shoots out of the edge and tips back, a rat riding the far end

u1.n: Rope Swing: rats on hanging ropes swing out hard and drop back

u2.n: Hold Gnaw: rats lunge off the edge teeth first, wood shavings falling from the gnawed hold

p.u3: Rigging Hold: a square of tarred ratlines holds along the edge, rat eyes glinting through the mesh

b0.n: Rope-Gnaw Snap: the crew races nose to tail along the edge, frayed rope fibres left behind

b1.n: Bilge Splash: bilge water slops off in heavy green drops that splat into a dark pool

b2.n: Tarred Crew Hide: tarred rigging lines the edge, a black tar gloss flicking over it

b3.n: Mutiny Rope Tug: rats hang on ropes at spots tied together, tugging the line

sea-otter-bandit.notes: A pale-faced sea otter with a bandit mask that floats on its back in the kelp, cracks shellfish on a stone on its tummy and keeps a favourite pebble in its armpit pocket; steals pails.

u0.n: Rock Crack: a ridged clam slams out, gapes pink and cracks in two, white shards flying

p.u1: Kelp Wrap: kelp fronds loop round masked otter heads that roll out and back, bladders bobbing

u2.n: Pebble Pocket: a smooth pebble glints at one spot, a furry fold closes over it, and it turns up somewhere else

p.u3: Tummy Anvil: otters float out on their backs and bring a clam down on the stone on their tummy, crack marks

b0.n: Shellfish Crack: clams are flung off the edge and crack open, bubbles

p.b1: Tummy Smash: otters lunge off the edge on their backs, paws smashing down on the tummy stone

b2.n: Otter Fur Coat: masked heads wrapped in kelp line the edge, drifting on the swell

b3.n: Pail Snatch: pebbles and loot hang at spots tied by a line, snatched one by one

bog-leech.notes: A dark teal-green bog leech that loops along sucker to sucker in murky water, latches on and drinks until it is fat; slime strings everywhere.

u0.n: Latch: sucker rings open, the three white jaws bite, and red beads drip off the edge

u1.n: Slick: leeches loop out and back over a slime trail

p.u2: Drain: fat leeches swell red with blood and rise off the edge, a drop at the tail
p.u3: Mire Slide: looping leeches hang at spots tied by slime strings, arching and stretching

b0.n: Murk Gulp: a sucker ring gulps out of the edge, a cloud of murk blooming

p.b1: Wriggle Surge: leeches arch and fling themselves off the edge in loops

b2.n: Slimy Sheath: leeches lie along the edge in a slimy sheath, a wet sheen flicking

b3.n: Murky Hideaway: leeches loop from spot to spot and vanish into a murk cloud

giant-mire-leech.notes: A boot-length, black, glossy, ridged leech of the deep mire: its huge back heaves up out of the bog like a log, hooks in and hauls in the rain.

u0.n: Bog Hook: the ridged black back heaves out of the edge and hooks, mud clods flung

u1.n: Muddy Coil: black leech coils hang at spots tied by mud strings, looping slowly

u2.n: Thick Hide: glossy ridged backs line the edge and breathe, a wet white gloss along the ridges

u3.n: Suck Dry: bloated leeches swell red and drop off the edge, heavy with blood

b0.n: Boot-Length Latch: a huge sucker ring lunges off the edge, three white jaws, a red bead

b1.n: Rain-Haul Heave: the great back heaves out in the rain and slaps down, raindrops flicked

b2.n: Black Blubber Coat: the ridged back lies along the edge over a glossy wet trail

b3.n: Mire Clutch Lurch: sucker rings clutch at spots tied by slime, lurching

tiger-leech.notes: An orange-and-brown striped rainforest leech that waits on wet leaf tips and drops onto whatever passes; often two drop at once.

u0.n: Stripe Latch: orange sucker rings dart off the edge and bite, a red bead

u1.n: Leaf Drop: striped leeches let go of the leaf tips and drop off the edge, dew falling with them

u2.n: Skin Wrap: a row of leaf tips holds along the edge, striped leeches hanging like a curtain, dew running

p.u3: Twin Drop: leaf tips blink from spot to spot, two striped leeches dangling from each

b0.n: Leech Latch Bite: sucker rings lunge off the edge and bite, wet dew flicked

p.b1: Wet-Leaf Drop: dripping leaf tips swing off the edge, a leech stretching from each

b2.n: Striped Slick Armour: striped leeches lie looped along the edge, a slick sheen

p.b3: Twin-Drop Pull: leeches dangle from leaf tips at spots tied by a silk of slime, pulling

saltmarsh-leech.notes: A grey-green, salt-dusted leech of brackish marsh pools: it swims in an S wave, salt grains on its back, regrows lost segments and bristles with salt crust.

u0.n: Salt Latch: a sucker ring runs the length of the edge and clamps on, salt glinting

u1.n: Marsh Mend: fresh leeches swim up out of the brine, bubbles rising (regrow)

p.u2: Brine Slick: cubic salt crystals push out of the edge like spikes, a corner flashing

u3.n: Gorge Bite: a bloated leech slams out, red belly showing, and drops back

b0.n: Marsh-Sea Latch: sucker rings lunge off the edge and bite

b1.n: Brackish Splash: S-swimming leeches fling off the edge in a brackish splash

b2.n: Salt Sheen Slick: a salt crust holds along the edge, white glints

p.b3: Brine Drag: swimming leeches hang at spots tied together, dragging through the brine

garfish.notes: A long silver-green garfish with needle jaws full of teeth and bony diamond scales: it skims just under the surface and leaps out flashing.

p.u0: Scale Plate: bony diamond scale plates line the edge, a white shine walking across them

u1.n: Needle Cover: needle jaws push out of the edge like spikes, tooth rows glinting

p.u2: Needle Jab: a garfish shoots the length of the edge needle first; the chain skips across in three leaps

u3.n: Glint Leap: garfish arc out of the water nose up, flash at the top and dive, splash rings

p.b0: Needle Beak Snap: needle jaws lunge off the edge and snap

b1.n: Shiny Leap: silver gars leap off the edge, a white glint at the top of the arc

b2.n: Bony Scale Plate: diamond scales line up along the edge, a sheen flicking over them

b3.n: Surface Glint: leaping gars flash at one spot of the surface after another
